components.name: userTask
components.description: A task that requires human intervention. Users interact with 'user tasks' via a task management system
components.usage: Use this task type when a task in the process flow requires manual action by a user. It typically involves human interaction, such as reviewing a document, approving a request, or entering data.

requiredInputs.name: taskName
requiredInputs.description: Name of the eTask for identification and display purposes

requiredInputs.name: taskDescription
requiredInputs.description: Detailed description of what the user needs to do in this task

requiredInputs.name: sourceSystemName
requiredInputs.description: Source system or process that generated this task

requiredInputs.name: taskPriority
requiredInputs.description: Priority level of the task

requiredInputs.name: taskDeadline
requiredInputs.description: Expected completion date and time for the task in date format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) or  duration (e.g. P{days}DT{hours}H{minutes}M)

requiredInputs.name: maximumActiveTasks
requiredInputs.description: Maximum number of active user tasks allowed to run concurrently

generatedOutputs.name: reasonCode
generatedOutputs.description: Reason code indicating how the task was completed. Useful for determining approval outcomes (e.g., 'APPROVED' vs 'REJECTED') or other completion reasons

generatedOutputs.name: comment
generatedOutputs.description: The comment entered by the user who completed the task

generatedOutputs.name: taskIdentifier
generatedOutputs.description: Unique reference identifier for the completed task instance. Useful for tracking, auditing, or correlating this specific task execution with external systems

components.name: serviceTask
components.description: A task performed by an external software service. Typically a REST call to GET/PUT/POST/DELETE
components.usage: Use service tasks when a task in the process flow can be automated and executed by a software service or application without direct human involvement. It often involves invoking external systems, performing calculations, or executing predefined functions

requiredInputs.name: serviceUrl
requiredInputs.description: Direct HTTP/HTTPS URL of the target service (e.g., https://api.example.com). Use this when the service endpoint is known and accessible via a direct URL

requiredInputs.name: uriPath
requiredInputs.description: Specific URI path to append to the location identifier

requiredInputs.name: httpMethod
requiredInputs.description: HTTP Method of the request to be invoked on the REST service called by this task

requiredInputs.name: headers
requiredInputs.description: List of request headers to be used with the REST request

properties.name: headerExpression
properties.description: Header value used for the HTTP request. Can be a constant value or an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: queryParams
requiredInputs.description: List of query parameters for the request URL

properties.name: parameterExpression
properties.description: Parameter value used for the HTTP request. It has to be an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: inputExpression
requiredInputs.description: Provide a simple expression to resolve the body of the HTTP request (e.g getVariable('requestDetails')). Use this ONLY for simple variable references or expressions without multi-line logic. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: inputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to compute or transform the body of the HTTP request. Use this when the input requires multi-line logic, variable manipulation, control flow, or complex transformations. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: outputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to process the response from the server (e.g handle status code and throw exceptions). The returned object will be available in a `response` variable with response.statusLine.statusCode, response.request.uri and response.entity available directly without any additional parsing

properties.name: callSubprocess
properties.description: Boolean to determine if subprocess should be invoked

generatedOutputs.name: statusCode
generatedOutputs.description: HTTP status code returned by the service

components.name: scriptTask
components.description: A task that executes internal Groovy script logic with no external API calls.
components.usage: Use ONLY when all logic is fully internal — no external API endpoint is called and no HTTP request is made. For any step that calls an external service or API, use serviceTask or sendTask. Do NOT use if the step involves any outbound HTTP call.

requiredInputs.name: script
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script code to execute

components.name: callActivity
components.description: A task that allows the current process to call another process from within its execution.
components.usage: Use call activity tasks to call another BPMN process by id. It should only be used if an id to the external process is provided.

requiredInputs.name: calledElement
requiredInputs.description: The process id to be called

requiredInputs.name: inputMapping
requiredInputs.description: Variables to be sent to Called Element (the external process) as payload data. E.g, to send payload.myVariable, source expression should be  getVariable('myVariable')  and target should be payload.someVariable. payload.someVariable is then accessible in the external process (the called element)

properties.name: source
properties.description: The source of the data to send to the external process, e.g. payload.myVariable

properties.name: sourceExpression
properties.description: The source expression to send to the external process, e.g.  getVariable('myVariable')

properties.name: target
properties.description: The target data on the external process that captures the data sent from the current process, e.g. payload.someVariable

requiredInputs.name: outputMapping
requiredInputs.description: Variable to be received back from the external process call (the called element). E.g, to use payload.myVariable from the external process, the source expression should be  getVariable('myVariable') . Keep the target as a variable that can be used in this this BPMN. The target variable is directly accessible and can be stored onto payload by persisting in a script task by using `payload.foo = targetVariable.`

properties.name: source
properties.description: The source of the data coming from the external process, e.g. payload.myVariable

properties.name: sourceExpression
properties.description: The source expression coming from the external process, e.g.  getVariable('myVariable')

properties.name: target
properties.description: The target data from the external process that captures the data from the external process to be used in the current process, e.g. targetVariable

requiredInputs.name: businessKey
requiredInputs.description: A boolean expression which gives the user search capabilities for the child process based on the business key. Is set to true by default.

components.name: manualTask
components.description: A task that should be used when a series of manual actions are to be performed external to the process by humans or to be used as a fallback when other bpmn components nodes do not fulfil the request
components.usage: Use manual tasks when the actions require human intervention in external systems outside the process or when explicitly mentioned as a manual task. It can also be used a fallback when other bpmn component nodes do not fulfil the request as a last resort.

components.name: businessRuleTask
components.description: A task that executes a business rule or decision logic linked to a decision application/decision id
components.usage: Use business rule tasks when a task in the process flow involves executing business rules or decision logic. It allows you to define and execute business rules or decision tables to determine the flow of the process based on certain conditions or criteria. Only use this when a decision application id or decision id is provided.

requiredInputs.name: executionEngine
requiredInputs.description: Execution engine for rule evaluation

requiredInputs.name: applicationId
requiredInputs.description: ID of the Application

requiredInputs.name: ruleName
requiredInputs.description: Rule Name of the rule to be executed

requiredInputs.name: ruleVersion
requiredInputs.description: Rule Version of the rule to be executed

requiredInputs.name: factTypesExpression
requiredInputs.description: Expression to be used to resolve the FactTypes of the rule. Specify either an FactTypes Expression or a FactTypes Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: factTypesScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to resolve the FactTypes of the rule. Specify either an FactTypes Expression or a FactTypes Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: metadataExpression
requiredInputs.description: Expression to be used to resolve the Metadata of the rule. Specify either an Metadata Expression or a Metadata Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: metadataScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to resolve the Metadata of the rule. Specify either an Metadata Expression or a Metadata Script, but not both

requiredInputs.name: outputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to process the response from the server (e.g handle status code or throw exceptions). The response object will be available in a `response` variable with response.statusLine.statusCode, response.request.uri and response.entity

components.name: subprocessCallNode
components.description: An inline subprocess call node that invokes a separately-defined subprocess by its identifier. This is the only correct mechanism for calling a subprocess from the main process flow (i.e. do not use a script or service task to call the subprocess node but use a subprocessCallNode element type).
components.usage: Use when the process flow must invoke a subprocess defined as a separate model. EVERY inline (triggeredByEvent=false) subprocess referenced by the process (e.g. a 'call subprocess SPn' step in the request, or an existing SPn / subprocessCallNode reference) MUST be invoked by EXACTLY ONE subprocessCallNode connected inline in the main flow. The subProcessId MUST exactly match the subprocess identifier shown in the high-level model (e.g. 'SP1', 'SP2'). Connect it inline with both inbound and outbound connections. Do NOT use scriptTask, serviceTask, or any other task type as a placeholder for a subprocess call — only this element type is recognised as a subprocess call point. Do NOT rename or alter the subProcessId. Event subprocesses (triggeredByEvent=true, started by a message/timer/error/conditional event) are NOT invoked this way and must NOT have a subprocessCallNode.

requiredInputs.name: subProcessId
requiredInputs.description: The identifier of the subprocess to invoke. Must exactly match the subprocess identifier from the high-level model (e.g. 'SP1', 'SP2'). Do NOT use the subprocess display name here. Use only the short identifier.

requiredInputs.name: subProcessName
requiredInputs.description: Human-readable name of the subprocess being called.

components.name: sendTask
components.description: A task that posts or sends data to an external system via a configured API endpoint.
components.usage: Use ONLY when an external API endpoint (serviceUrl or discoveryPath) is available and the step sends/posts data outbound. If no API endpoint is provided or known, use scriptTask instead. Do NOT use sendTask for steps that merely transform data or run logic without calling an external API as this is a scriptTask.

requiredInputs.name: serviceUrl
requiredInputs.description: Direct HTTP/HTTPS URL of the target service (e.g., https://api.example.com). Use this when the service endpoint is known and accessible via a direct URL

requiredInputs.name: uriPath
requiredInputs.description: Specific URI path to append to the location identifier

requiredInputs.name: httpMethod
requiredInputs.description: HTTP Method of the request to be invoked on the REST service called by this task

requiredInputs.name: headers
requiredInputs.description: List of request headers to be used with the REST request

properties.name: headerExpression
properties.description: Header value used for the HTTP request. Can be a constant value or an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: queryParams
requiredInputs.description: List of query parameters for the request URL

properties.name: parameterExpression
properties.description: Parameter value used for the HTTP request. It has to be an expression to be evaluated at runtime

requiredInputs.name: inputExpression
requiredInputs.description: Provide a simple expression to resolve the body of the HTTP request (e.g getVariable('requestDetails')). Use this ONLY for simple variable references or expressions without multi-line logic. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: inputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to compute or transform the body of the HTTP request. Use this when the input requires multi-line logic, variable manipulation, control flow, or complex transformations. Not required for GET requests. Specify either inputExpression OR inputScript, but not both

requiredInputs.name: outputScript
requiredInputs.description: Groovy script to process the response from the server (e.g handle status code and throw exceptions). The response object will be available in a `response` variable with response.statusLine.statusCode, response.request.uri and response.entity

components.name: receiveTask
components.description: A task that waits for an inbound machine-to-machine message or signal from an external system.
components.usage: Use ONLY when the process must pause until an external SYSTEM (not a human) sends a specific message or signal. Do NOT use when waiting for a human or user to act — use userTask or a message intermediate catch event instead. Do NOT use when waiting based on elapsed time — use a timer intermediate catch event instead.

requiredInputs.name: messageId
requiredInputs.description: ID of a message to listen for

requiredInputs.name: availabilityRuleScript
requiredInputs.description: A Groovy script that specifies control of who can call this Receive Task

components.name: startEvent
components.description: Represents the beginning of a process flow.
components.usage: Place at the start of the process flow to indicate where it begins. Can have triggers like message, timer, or signal.  Only one per process

components.name: messageStartEvent
components.description: A start event for a subprocess that is triggered when a specified message is received. Used to start event-driven subprocesses.
components.usage: Use as the start event inside a subprocess when it is triggered by an event thrown by another task from the main process or an external system. The subprocess will be activated when the specified message is received. Can be interrupting (cancels the main process) or non-interrupting (runs in parallel with the main process).

requiredInputs.name: messageRef
requiredInputs.description: The name or identifier of the message this start event listens for

requiredInputs.name: isInterrupting
requiredInputs.description: If true, the event subprocess interrupts the main process. If false, it runs in parallel without interrupting the main process.

components.name: timerStartEvent
components.description: A start event for a subprocess that is triggered after a specified duration or at a specific date/time. Used to start event-driven subprocesses on a schedule or delay.
components.usage: Use as the start event inside a subprocess when it is triggered by an event thrown by another task from the main process. The subprocess will be activated when the timer fires. Can be interrupting or non-interrupting.

requiredInputs.name: timeDuration
requiredInputs.description: ISO 8601 duration expression for when the event should trigger (e.g. PT1H). Specify either timeDuration or timeDate, not both.

requiredInputs.name: timeDate
requiredInputs.description: ISO 8601 date/time expression for a specific point in time when the event should trigger. Specify either timeDuration or timeDate, not both.

requiredInputs.name: isInterrupting
requiredInputs.description: If true, the event subprocess interrupts the main process. If false, it runs in parallel without interrupting the main process.

components.name: errorStartEvent
components.description: A start event for a subprocess that is triggered when a specific error is thrown within the parent process. Always interrupting. Used to start error-handling event subprocesses.
components.usage: Use as the start event inside a subprocess when it is triggered by an event thrown by another task from the main process. The subprocess will be activated when the specified error is thrown. This is always going to interrupt and cancel the main process flow.

requiredInputs.name: errorRef
requiredInputs.description: The error code or identifier this start event catches. If empty, catches all errors.

generatedOutputs.name: errorCode
generatedOutputs.description: The error code of the caught error

generatedOutputs.name: errorMessage
generatedOutputs.description: The error message of the caught error

components.name: conditionalStartEvent
components.description: A start event for a subprocess that is triggered when a condition evaluates to true. Used to start event-driven subprocesses based on data conditions.
components.usage: Use as the start event inside a subprocess when it is triggered by an event thrown by another task from the main process. The subprocess will be activated when the condition becomes true. Can be interrupting or non-interrupting.

requiredInputs.name: conditionExpression
requiredInputs.description: A boolean expression that is evaluated to determine whether this subprocess should be started

requiredInputs.name: isInterrupting
requiredInputs.description: If true, the event subprocess interrupts the main process. If false, it runs in parallel without interrupting the main process.

components.name: endEvent
components.description: Denotes the completion of a process flow.
components.usage: Place at the end of the process flow to indicate where it ends. Can have outcomes like message, error, or termination. At least one required per process

components.name: terminateEndEvent
components.description: An end event that terminates the entire process immediately, including all active branches and tasks. Unlike a normal endEvent which only ends the current path, terminateEndEvent stops everything.
components.usage: An end event that terminates the entire process immediately, including all active branches and tasks. Unlike a normal endEvent which only ends the current path, terminateEndEvent stops everything.

components.name: errorEndEvent
components.description: An end event that throws an error. Typically used inside subprocesses to signal a failure to the main process.  The error can be caught by an errorBoundaryEvent on the enclosing subprocess, or by an errorStartEvent in an event subprocess. If uncaught, the main process ends with an error state.
components.usage: An end event that throws an error. Typically used inside subprocesses to signal a failure to the main process.  The error can be caught by an errorBoundaryEvent on the enclosing subprocess, or by an errorStartEvent in an event subprocess. If uncaught, the main process ends with an error state.

requiredInputs.name: errorRef
requiredInputs.description: The error code or identifier of the error to throw

requiredInputs.name: errorMessage
requiredInputs.description: A human-readable description of the error

components.name: messageEndEvent
components.description: An end event that sends a message when the process flow reaches it. Used to notify external systems or other processes that this process path has completed.
components.usage: Use when the process needs to send a message to an external participant or another process upon completion of a flow path. The message is published when the end event is reached.

requiredInputs.name: messageRef
requiredInputs.description: The name or identifier of the message to send when this end event is reached

components.name: exclusiveGateway
components.description: Allows branching based on a condition or merging from multiple paths
components.usage: Use when the process flow can branch to multiple nodes, but ONLY ONE of the paths can be followed. Each outgoing connection flow has a condition which must be met for the process to take that path. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways

requiredInputs.name: default
requiredInputs.description: Identifier of a default target node if no conditions are met

requiredInputs.name: conditions
requiredInputs.description: List of conditions for each outgoing path. Each condition includes the target node identifier and the condition expression to evaluate. Merge gateways with one outgoing path can have empty condition expression

properties.name: targetNodeId
properties.description: Identifier of the target node for this condition

properties.name: conditionExpression
properties.description: Boolean expression used to evaluate whether this path should be taken

components.name: inclusiveGateway
components.description: Allows branching based on a condition or merging from multiple paths
components.usage: Use when the process flow can branch to multiple nodes, and MULTIPLE paths can be followed simultaneously. Each outgoing connection flow has a condition which must be met for the process to take that path. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways.

requiredInputs.name: default
requiredInputs.description: Identifier of a default target node if no conditions are met.

requiredInputs.name: conditions
requiredInputs.description: List of conditions for each outgoing path. Each condition includes the target node identifier and the condition expression to evaluate

properties.name: targetNodeId
properties.description: Identifier of the target node for this condition

properties.name: conditionExpression
properties.description: Boolean expression used to evaluate whether this path should be taken

components.name: parallelGateway
components.description: Allows diverging into, or converging from, multiple parallel paths
components.usage: Use when the process flow should split into multiple parallel paths or merge from multiple parallel paths simultaneously. All outgoing sequence flows are followed in parallel, and all incoming sequence flows must complete before proceeding. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways

components.name: eventBasedGateway
components.description: Allows pausing the process flow and waiting until a subsequent catching event is triggered. At that point, the process proceeds.
components.usage: Use whenever a workflow is required to wait for two or more events at the same time, for instance a message to be received or the passage of time to reach a certain point. Each gateway must be EITHER a split OR a merge - never both. If you need to merge and then split, use two separate gateways

components.name: processConfig
components.description: Use this node to represent a configuration of the process. This node has no effect besides documentation. It should not have any outputs or connections to other nodes as it will not be rendered as a node in the executable model
components.usage: Use this node to represent a configuration of the process. This node has no effect besides documentation. It should not have any outputs or connections to other nodes as it will not be rendered as a node in the executable model.

requiredInputs.name: processId
requiredInputs.description: Unique identifier for the process instance

requiredInputs.name: processName
requiredInputs.description: Name of the process appearing to the user. This should contain fixed, contextual information to allow instances of a process to be distinguished

requiredInputs.name: processDescription
requiredInputs.description: Name of the process appearing to the user. This should contain fixed, contextual information to allow instances of a process to be distinguished

requiredInputs.name: sourceSystemName
requiredInputs.description: Source system generated this process

requiredInputs.name: processPriority
requiredInputs.description: Priority level of the process.

requiredInputs.name: processDeadline
requiredInputs.description: Expected completion date and time for the process in date format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) or  duration (e.g. P{days}DT{hours}H{minutes}M)

requiredInputs.name: maximumActiveProcesses
requiredInputs.description: Maximum number of active processes allowed before throttling

components.name: subProcess
components.description: Use this node to represent a subprocess. A subprocess represents a collection of tasks that exist solely for handling a specific case beyond the main process. It is an action or series of actions that can be called at any point and as many times from the main process or as part of the main process. A subprocess can be triggered from a task in the main process, an external system that calls the subprocess through a message event, or it can be part of the main flow to isolate a series of actions (so that it can be made iterable for example)
components.usage: Use this node to represent a subprocess. A subprocess represents a collection of tasks that exist solely for handling a specific case beyond the main process. It is an action or series of actions that can be called at any point and as many times from the main process or as part of the main process. A subprocess can be triggered from a task in the main process, an external system that calls the subprocess through a message event, or it can be part of the main flow to isolate a series of actions (so that it can be made iterable for example)

requiredInputs.name: subProcessId
requiredInputs.description: Unique identifier for the subprocess instance

requiredInputs.name: subProcessName
requiredInputs.description: Human-readable name of the subprocess being called or defined. Name of the subprocess appearing to the user. This should contain contextual information to allow instances of a process to be distinguished

requiredInputs.name: subProcessDescription
requiredInputs.description: Name of the subprocess appearing to the user. This should contain contextual information to allow instances of a process to be distinguished

requiredInputs.name: triggeredByEvent
requiredInputs.description: If triggeredByEvent is true, the subprocess can be triggered by an event thrown by another node or an external event. If false, the subprocess is connected to the main process.

components.name: timerBoundaryEvent
components.description: A boundary event attached to a task or subprocess that triggers after a specified duration or at a specific date/time. When it is an interrupting event (cancelActivity=true in the events[] definition), the attached task/subprocess is cancelled. When non-interrupting, the attached task/subprocess continues and a parallel flow is started.
components.usage: Embed in the 'events' array of a task or subprocess node. Use interrupting mode to cancel the task after a timeout (e.g. cancel a user task after 7 days). Use non-interrupting mode to trigger a parallel action without cancelling the task (e.g. send a reminder email after 3 days). Do NOT add as a standalone node — always embed in the parent task's events[].

requiredInputs.name: cancelActivity
requiredInputs.description: Whether this boundary event is interrupting (true) or non-interrupting (false). When interrupting, the attached task/subprocess is cancelled when the event triggers. Defaults to true.

requiredInputs.name: timeDuration
requiredInputs.description: ISO 8601 duration expression for when the event should trigger (e.g. PT1H). Specify either timeDuration or timeDate, NOT both.

requiredInputs.name: timeDate
requiredInputs.description: ISO 8601 date/time expression for a specific point in time when the event should trigger (e.g. 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z). Specify either timeDuration or timeDate, NOT both.

components.name: messageBoundaryEvent
components.description: A boundary event attached to a task or subprocess that triggers when a specified message is received. When it is an interrupting event (cancelActivity=true in the events[] definition), the attached task/subprocess is cancelled. When non-interrupting, the attached task/subprocess continues and a parallel flow is started.
components.usage: Embed in the 'events' array of a task or subprocess node. Use interrupting mode when an external message means the task is no longer needed (e.g. customer cancels a request). Use non-interrupting mode to handle additional information without stopping the current task. Do NOT add as a standalone node.

requiredInputs.name: cancelActivity
requiredInputs.description: Whether this boundary event is interrupting (true) or non-interrupting (false). When interrupting, the attached task/subprocess is cancelled when the event triggers. Defaults to true.

requiredInputs.name: messageRef
requiredInputs.description: The name or identifier of the message this event listens for

components.name: errorBoundaryEvent
components.description: A boundary event attached to a task or subprocess that triggers when a specific error is thrown. Error boundary events are always interrupting — they cancel the attached task/subprocess.
components.usage: Embed in the 'events' array of a task or subprocess node. Always set cancelActivity=true (error boundary events are always interrupting). Use to catch errors thrown by the attached task or subprocess. Do NOT add as a standalone node.

requiredInputs.name: errorRef
requiredInputs.description: The error code or identifier of the error this event catches. If empty, catches all errors.

generatedOutputs.name: errorCode
generatedOutputs.description: The error code of the caught error

generatedOutputs.name: errorMessage
generatedOutputs.description: The error message of the caught error

components.name: conditionalBoundaryEvent
components.description: A boundary event attached to a task or subprocess that triggers when a specified condition evaluates to true. When interrupting, the attached task/subprocess is cancelled. When non-interrupting, it continues and a parallel flow is started.
components.usage: Embed in the 'events' array of a task or subprocess node. Use when a data condition should trigger an alternative or parallel flow while a task is active. Do NOT add as a standalone node.

requiredInputs.name: cancelActivity
requiredInputs.description: Whether this boundary event is interrupting (true) or non-interrupting (false). When interrupting, the attached task/subprocess is cancelled when the event triggers. Defaults to true.

requiredInputs.name: conditionExpression
requiredInputs.description: A boolean expression that is evaluated to determine whether this event should trigger

components.name: messageIntermediateCatchEvent
components.description: An intermediate catch event placed in the process flow that pauses execution and waits for a specified message to be received before continuing.
components.usage: Use in the main process flow when the process should wait for an external message before continuing

requiredInputs.name: messageRef
requiredInputs.description: The name or identifier of the message this event listens for

components.name: messageIntermediateThrowEvent
components.description: An intermediate throw event placed in the process flow that sends a message and then continues. Used to signal other processes.
components.usage: Use in the main process flow when the process needs to send a message to another process or external system and then continue execution.

requiredInputs.name: messageRef
requiredInputs.description: The name or identifier of the message to send

components.name: timerIntermediateCatchEvent
components.description: An intermediate catch event placed in the process flow that pauses execution for a specified duration or until a specific date/time before continuing.
components.usage: Use in the main process flow when the process should wait for a period of time before continuing

requiredInputs.name: timeDuration
requiredInputs.description: ISO 8601 duration expression for how long to wait (e.g. PT1H). Specify either timeDuration or timeDate, not both.

requiredInputs.name: timeDate
requiredInputs.description: ISO 8601 date/time expression for a specific point in time to wait until. Specify either timeDuration or timeDate, not both.

components.name: conditionalIntermediateCatchEvent
components.description: An intermediate catch event placed in the process flow that pauses execution and waits until a specified condition evaluates to true before continuing.
components.usage: Use when the process should wait for a data condition to become true before continuing

requiredInputs.name: conditionExpression
requiredInputs.description: A boolean expression that is evaluated to determine whether this event should trigger
